**Class** in the `Latiprimere.Windows` namespace, from the [Latiprimere.Windows](/docs/reference/#latiprimerewindows) package.

```csharp
public sealed class WindowsOptions
```

Configures printing through the Windows print spooler.

## Constructors

```csharp
public WindowsOptions()
```

## Properties

### AllowAnyPrinterName

```csharp
public bool AllowAnyPrinterName { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets a value indicating whether a printer identifier may name any printer, including one on a print server the user hasn't connected to (`windows:\\server\printer`). Defaults to `false`: a name with a backslash or a comma is looked up only if Windows lists it, as a local printer or as a connection the user already made.

Looking up `\\server\printer` contacts that server, and Windows may sign in to it with the application's account, sending a response that can be relayed or cracked. A comma opens special spooler handles, such as `name,Job 5`. When identifiers can come from outside the application, such as from a web request, allowing any name would let others make it contact any host.

Turn this on to look up printers on servers that aren't connected yet, when every identifier the application looks up is trusted. Plain local printer names work either way.

### IppPrinterUris

```csharp
public IDictionary<string, Uri> IppPrinterUris { get; }
```

Gets the IPP URIs of Windows queues, by queue name (not case-sensitive), for [WindowsOptions.PrintPdfOverIpp](/docs/reference/latiprimere-windows/windowsoptions/#printpdfoveripp).

Needed for queues whose port doesn't give the printer's address, such as WSD and Standard TCP/IP ports, as Latiprimere doesn't guess it. Each URI must be an absolute `ipp`, `ipps`, `http` or `https` URI, such as `ipp://192.168.1.20/ipp/print`; the print system refuses others when created.

### MaxRenderDpi

```csharp
public int? MaxRenderDpi { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets the highest resolution, in dots per inch, at which PDF pages are rendered before they are sent to the printer, or `null` to render at the printer's own resolution. Defaults to `null`.

On Windows, PDF pages are rendered to images and drawn through the printer driver. A printer at 600 DPI gets 600 DPI images, which take time and memory. Below its resolution, pages are rendered at this value and scaled up to the printer's, so jobs take less time and memory, but small text and fine lines are softer. Printing 100 A4 pages to Microsoft Print to PDF at 600 DPI took 66 seconds and 225 MiB at full resolution, and 36 seconds and 130 MiB capped at 300 DPI.

A value at or above the printer's resolution changes nothing. Raw jobs aren't rendered, so this doesn't affect them.

**Exceptions**

- [ArgumentOutOfRangeException](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.argumentoutofrangeexception): The value is zero or negative.

### PrintPdfOverIpp

```csharp
public bool PrintPdfOverIpp { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets a value indicating whether to send PDF jobs straight to the printer over IPP when Latiprimere knows or can find the queue's IPP printer. Defaults to `false`.

A PDF sent over IPP reaches the printer as it is, instead of as a picture of each page drawn through the driver: it prints faster, with sharp text, and the job reports how it really ended. A job goes this way only when all of these hold, and otherwise through the Windows queue as before:

- the queue's IPP URI is in [WindowsOptions.IppPrinterUris](/docs/reference/latiprimere-windows/windowsoptions/#ippprinteruris); or the queue was added by URL, so its port is named after the printer's address; or it is on a WSD port, and a printer on the network announces itself over mDNS with the UUID the port records, and reports that UUID when asked;
- the queue isn't on a print server;
- the printer says it accepts PDF, or, with a PDF rasteriser, PWG raster or Apple raster, which is asked at its first PDF job. A PDF it can't take is rendered and sent in one of those, at the printer's resolution limited by [WindowsOptions.MaxRenderDpi](/docs/reference/latiprimere-windows/windowsoptions/#maxrenderdpi);
- the job doesn't set [PrintOptions.OutputFile](/docs/reference/latiprimere-abstractions/printoptions/#outputfile), an [PrintOptions.InputTray](/docs/reference/latiprimere-abstractions/printoptions/#inputtray), or a `windows:` vendor option.

Such jobs bypass the Windows queue: they don't appear in its queue window, and its pause, permissions, pooling and accounting don't apply to them. Their job IDs are the printer's, and `ipp:` vendor options are sent with them. If the printer can't be reached, the job goes through the Windows queue, which holds it until the printer is back. Finding a WSD queue's printer listens on the network for up to two seconds at its first PDF job; a printer not found isn't searched for again for five minutes.
